significance.justification: A verified-true result would license the form-(iii) conclusion that recursive subliminal transfer follows measurable population dynamics: trait strength amplifies when the "per-generation transfer gain exceeds 1," decays when it is below 1, and changes identity as "the transferred steering direction slowly rotates." This establishes both a phenomenon—long-run amplification, extinction, or drift—and a partial mechanism linking those trajectories to transfer gain and steering-direction stability, thereby predicting later generations rather than merely showing that a trait is represented; Cloud et al.'s 2025 Subliminal Learning work makes persistence through model-generated data a concrete concern, so whether one-step transmission composes is load-bearing. The outcomes are determinate despite being bundled: failure to find gain-dependent trajectories or direction-coupled drift would rule out the proposed dynamical extrapolation from one-step transfer, although the spontaneous-emergence clause is less sharply specified. In the topic-substitution check, merely restating "extend subliminal learning" would not support this score; the gain threshold, longitudinal predictive coupling, and drift law are specific additions false of the median single-transfer hypothesis.

reach.justification: The transferable handles are the claimed "per-generation transfer gain," "amplification/extinction thresholds," and steering-direction stability, which together could forecast whether a recursive training chain will amplify or purge a trait. This is ex ante after early generations rather than merely post hoc: estimating gain and rotation supplies an action window before "runaway" amplification or entrenchment over later generations. After re-extraction on another compatible model, the conclusion predicts a relation—gain above or below one determines the trajectory—rather than only prescribing a search for an unspecified direction; its asserted scope is recursive model distillation broadly, with auditors and engineers operating model-generated-data pipelines as plausible downstream users. The topic-substitution check does not preserve this score: the reach comes from the named predictive quantities and threshold rule, not from the general importance of subliminal learning.
